extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in TikTok (users, researchers, policy observers)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and apply TikTok platform features, eligibility rules, moderation policies, and content/monetization constraints for creating or evaluating content on TikTok/Douyin. Useful for creators, parents, researchers, and moderators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video duration limits
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok hosts user-submitted videos, which range in duration from three seconds to 60 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators must conform to supported length ranges when producing content; different formats (short clips vs long-form) have different production and engagement expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account privacy defaults and per-video visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The mobile app allows users to set their accounts as 'private'. When first downloading the app, the user's account is public by default. Users can also set specific videos to either 'public', 'friends only', or 'private' regardless if the account is private or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators and evaluators should note default public visibility on new installs and the per-video controls for selective sharing; private content remains visible to TikTok (the company) even if blocked to other users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction/engagement settings (comments/messages/react/duet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can choose whether any other user, or only their 'friends', may interact with them through the app via comments, messages, or 'react' or 'duet' videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjusting these settings affects discoverability and collaboration; duet/react features depend on privacy choices of involved accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duet/react/stitch permission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'duet' feature is only able to be used if both parties adjust the privacy settings. Users can also use portions of other TikTok videos by creating a 'stitch'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators reusing others' content must respect original creators' privacy/permission settings; platform-level controls can prevent duets/stitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live feature eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Influencers often use the 'live' feature. This feature is only available for those who have at least 1,000 followers and are over 16 years old. If over 18, the user's followers can send virtual 'gifts' that can be later exchanged for money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts below thresholds cannot access live streaming; monetization via gifts requires being 18+ and meeting follower thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip/monetization eligibility and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Accounts of users that are of age, have at least 100,000 followers and agree to the terms can activate a 'Tip' button on their profile, which allows followers to tip any amount, starting from $1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization features have explicit age and follower-count thresholds; creators should meet terms/agreements to enable tipping and note minimum tip amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafts and posting workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos that users do not want to post yet can be stored in their 'drafts'. The user is allowed to see their 'drafts' and post when they find it fitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafts support iterative production; evaluators should consider draft visibility and later posting timing when assessing creator activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic recommendation criteria (For You page)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'For You' page on TikTok is an endless feed of videos that are recommended to users based on their activity on the app. TikTok monitors a wider array of behaviors during video viewing beyond likes, clicks, or follows; this comprehensive observation refines recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content creators should optimize for viewing behaviors (watch time, replays, completion) as the recommendation algorithm emphasizes these signals over simple likes/follows; researchers should note the broad set of behavioral signals used.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Heating' manual promotion practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'heating' tool allows TikTok to manually promote certain videos, comprising 1–2% of daily views. It is used to grow and diversify content and to promote brands, artists, and NGOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heating is an editorial/manual amplification mechanism with limited share of views; concerns exist about discretionary abuse (employees promoting own accounts) and the need for vetted approval/auditing in sensitive jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and external review commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: After increased scrutiny, TikTok said it is granting some outside experts access to the platform's anonymized data sets and protocols, including filters, keywords, criteria for heating, and source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External auditing and data-sharing commitments affect trust assessments; evaluators should consider the extent and limits of external access when judging transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content moderation / censorship policy themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal guidelines prohibit promotion of violence, separatism, and 'demonization of countries' and have been used to remove or suppress content on sensitive political and historical topics (e.g., Tiananmen, Falun Gong, human rights in Tibet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderation rules can be broad and non-transparent; creators addressing sensitive political topics risk suppression or takedown; policy critics note both global guidelines and localized/customized versions by region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted topics and demographic suppression concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations reported moderators were instructed to suppress posts from 'For You' recommendations if the users shown were deemed 'too ugly, poor, or disabled'. Consumption of alcohol, full or partial nudity, LGBT and intersex contents were restricted even in places where they are legal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content involving protected classes or sensitive portrayals may be disproportionately limited; creators and researchers should be aware of non-content-based suppression criteria and regional differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Douyin-specific content prohibitions (China)
rubrics_metrics.description: Douyin guidelines forbid live broadcasting by unregistered foreigners, 'feudal superstition', 'money worship', smoking and drinking, competitive eating by the 'already obese', 'toxic' slime, 'pornographic' ASMR such as ear-licking, and female anchors wearing revealing clothes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creators on Douyin face additional culturally and regulatorily specific prohibitions distinct from TikTok; cross-border creators should not assume identical rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family safety controls / Family Pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok announced a 'family safety mode' with screen time management, restricted mode, and an option to put a limit on direct messages. 'Family Pairing' provides parents and guardians with educational resources and control features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents and guardians can limit exposure and interaction for minors via these tools; evaluators of child-directed content should consider these constraints and available safety features.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM feed curation and reliability checks
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok introduced a dedicated STEM feed that works with Common Sense Networks to check for safety and age appropriateness and with the Poynter Institute for reliability of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized feeds may apply external verification and safety partners; creators posting educational STEM content should expect additional reliability and appropriateness scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and Creative Center limits
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok restricted the number of hashtags that can be searched under its Creative Center, saying it was 'misused to draw inaccurate conclusions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tooling and analytics access may be rate-limited or restricted; researchers relying on platform search tools should account for such limits and potential changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music licensing and availability constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has licensing deals with major music companies; disputes (e.g., Universal withdrawing catalogue) have caused music to become unavailable. Creators have criticized TikTok for not paying royalties to artists whose music is used on the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of copyrighted music is constrained by licensing agreements which can change availability; creators should verify song availability and rights—music removal can impact content strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and promotional restrictions (cosmetic surgery example)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has banned the advertising of cosmetic surgeries on the platform, though cosmetic surgeons may still reach audiences through unpaid posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising policy may prohibit some paid promotions while allowing organic/unpaid content; creators and advertisers must distinguish between paid ads (subject to bans) and organic posts (may still spread widely).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to harmful trends and enforcement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has taken measures to remove and prevent access to harmful trends (e.g., 'devious licks', the Kia Challenge) and faced legal and safety consequences tied to some trends (e.g., crashes and deaths tied to car-theft challenges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform enforcement can include removals and mitigation; creators should avoid participating in dangerous trends, and evaluators should consider platform actions when assessing risk and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software licensing compliance for platform tools
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok's Live Studio used code from the open-source OBS Studio; under the GNU GPL version 2, TikTok has obligations to make code available if it uses OBS code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform developers and third-party tool creators must comply with open-source license obligations; failure to do so can lead to public statements and compliance requirements.
